## HoeGekIsNL

Scores draw on one peer-reviewed article [@vanderkrieke2016], a project
description from the research centre [@mindwise2016] and the study website
[@hoegekis_web]. Only the abstract of the article was read, so data quality
(B5) was not assessed. Members of the public enrolled themselves and received
automatically generated personal reports, which met the items on mutual benefit
and return of results (B1, B2). The questions were set by the research team,
and no other public role is documented, so the case is classed as
crowdsourcing. The website still invites participants (D1 = ●), but no source
documents use of the findings by decision-makers (C3 = NR), so the verdict is
insufficient evidence. The enrolment of more than 200 minors despite an
adult-only rule is recorded under D2, where no harm was documented.
